entries.intro: A moderate week: a few real partner-style plays (Resy, Oura, Rove, Qantas and Cathay) plus one rising rival to watch (Bilt). Several items are copycat or counter plays, not net-new partners, so only the ones worth a team conversation made the cut.

items.what: Reservation platform that Amex owns, now paired with a reservation-linked rewards program.
items.signal: Amex launched Resy Rewards, giving 4 extra Membership Rewards points on dining reservations paid with an enrolled card. Restaurant eligibility looks limited and rollout is unclear.
items.why_fit: Ties card earn directly to booking behavior at restaurants affluent clients favor, and could be replicated with a non-Amex reservation or dining platform.
items.angle: A reservation-linked dining earn or access perk with a booking partner, positioned as a counter to Resy Rewards.

items.what: Maker of the Oura smart ring, a premium wearable.
items.signal: Oura Ring 5 is $299 in an early Black Friday sale, and Amex Platinum cardholders can bring it to $99 plus tax through November 30 via a card benefit. Sale end date and credit eligibility are not fully confirmed.
items.why_fit: A premium wellness hardware brand with a proven card-credit structure and strong fit with affluent, health-minded clients.
items.angle: A wellness or wearable statement credit or member price, positioned as a counter to the Platinum Oura offer.

items.what: Shopping offers platform that pays out in airline miles.
items.signal: Rove launched personalized shopping offers paying up to 25 miles per dollar spent.
items.why_fit: A card-linked or miles-linked offer engine could supply merchant offers without us building each merchant relationship one by one.
items.angle: Personalized merchant offers surfaced to premium cardholders, or a benchmark for our own offers strategy.

items.what: Rent-focused rewards platform and card program, now pushing into travel and events.
items.signal: Reportedly seeking an $18 billion valuation, and its December Rent Day adds a JetBlue Mosaic status challenge and a redemption bonus up to 100%. The valuation talks are unconfirmed.
items.why_fit: A fast-growing rival building partner-funded perks (airline status, concerts, redemption bonuses) aimed at younger affluent renters, a segment partners will chase.
items.angle: Partner-funded status matches or lifestyle events for renters and younger affluent clients, and a rival to track for partner overlap.

items.what: Global hotel loyalty program and a major US airline.
items.signal: Hyatt plans stackable awards, new Milestone Rewards and Delta perks, all launching in 2027.
items.why_fit: A hotel and airline tie-up signals where affluent travelers' loyalty is consolidating, and Hyatt has a strong premium guest base.
items.angle: Complementary hotel or airline benefits timed ahead of the 2027 rollout.

items.what: Private aviation provider offering fractional ownership and jet cards.
items.signal: NetJets was named official private aviation provider for the Hahnenkamm Races in Kitzbühel.
items.why_fit: A premium event sponsorship shows appetite for affluent audience reach, which suits top-tier card flight and experience benefits.
items.angle: Private aviation access or event-linked flight benefit for top-tier cardholders.

items.what: Bill-pay fintech that lets businesses pay bills by card for a 2.9% fee and earn transferable points.
items.signal: Adding Atmos Rewards support soon, which is not yet live.
items.why_fit: Turns otherwise uncardable business spend into points, relevant to small business and affluent owner clients.
items.angle: Business bill-pay earn partnership for premium business cardholders.
